due_when.clears_when: matched_random_intervention (and the two lane drivers) draw a causal control with a self-test showing a uniform-over-own-length draw is refused or flagged, and the affected landed records are re-graded

what: NON-CAUSAL MATCHED-RANDOM CONTROL. Drawing the random intervention's bar/check-in UNIFORMLY among a trade's own decision points uses the trade's final length (future information), so the control is not a policy a trader could run and its dR is biased. MEASURED in RQ-20261029-a7e1-02 (TD n=1831 trades, 2020-07..2026-10, 2000 draws): the uniform-bar random 50% partial close scored median +0.014..+0.026 R/trade and beat every fixed-bar variant in 100% of draws (beat fraction 0.0 for k=3/6/12/24); the a7e1-01 random arm (+0.0146 R, 29% maxDD cut) is the same artifact. Affected code: scripts/research/ml_am_partial_noninferior.py::random_arm, scripts/research/am_static_partial.py::random_books, and the SHARED scripts/research/intervention_controls.py::matched_random_intervention (B2: arr[rng.integers(0, len(arr))] over a trade's valid check-ins), which feeds desk_replay_driver and every unit declaring intervention_controls.matched_random. Fix: draw a causal policy -- at each check-in fire with the intervention's per-check-in hazard (or draw an offset from the intervention's own offset distribution and fire only if the trade is still open). Then re-grade the landed records whose verdict used R4/the random control and say which change. The a7e1-01 and a7e1-02 FAIL verdicts stand without R4 (each family also fails non-inferiority, R1, R2 or R3).
